chunks: And by this chain, from Al-Hasan ibn Yusuf, from Uthman ibn Jabalah, from Al-Darīs ibn Abd al-Malik, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: We are Quraysh, and our Shī‘ah are the Arabs, and our enemies are the Ajam (Persians/non-Arabs).

key_terms.الْعَجَمُ: The Ajam (non-Arabs, specifically Persians), identified here as the enemies.
key_terms.الْعَرَبُ: The Arabs, identified here as the group associated with the Shī‘ah.
key_terms.شِيعَتُنَا: Our Shī‘ah (followers/partisans), referring to the devoted followers of the Imams.
key_terms.قُرَيْشٌ: Quraysh, the tribe of the Prophet Muhammad, often used to denote the Ahl al-Bayt or their lineage.

ai.seo_question: Who are the Shī‘ah and enemies according to Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the sociological and theological boundaries of the Shī‘ah by identifying Quraysh as the leadership lineage, Arabs as the core followers, and Ajam (Persians/non-Arabs) as the adversaries. This classification reflects the early Shī‘a community's distinct identity formation within the broader Islamic polity, emphasizing tribal and ethnic affiliations as markers of loyalty and opposition. The statement underscores the historical context where Arab lineage was often associated with the Prophet’s household, while non-Ar-Arab converts, particularly Persians, were sometimes viewed with suspicion due to political tensions.
